title: Social-protection reform shows a measurable gap between legal entitlement and effective access
source_unit: International Labour Organization, ILO Global Flagship Programme on Building Social Protection Floors for All: Report of the second phase (2021-25), 2026
geography: 50 priority countries across Africa, the Americas, Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, and Europe and Central Asia, with programme-level global results

observations.period: 2021-2025; people-level impacts of the ILO Global Flagship Programme

denominator.unit: people affected by programme-supported legal coverage, effective coverage, adequacy, or comprehensiveness changes

total_impacted.value: 84,191,875 people experienced improvements in legal or effective coverage, benefit adequacy, or comprehensiveness during 2021-2025, against an ambition of 60 million

legal_coverage.value: 31.51 million people gained legal coverage, against an ambition of 20 million

effective_coverage.value: 23.81 million people gained effective coverage, below the 30 million ambition

adequacy_comprehensiveness.value: 28.87 million people experienced more comprehensive or adequate protection, against an ambition of 10 million

mechanism.value: legal entitlement can scale faster than registration, contribution collection, administration, and benefit delivery, creating a measurable de jure-to-de facto protection gap

observations.method: ILO programme results monitoring tool and project progress reports tracking legal coverage, effective coverage, benefit adequacy, and comprehensiveness across country interventions.
observations.uncertainty: These are programme-attributed results rather than population-wide causal estimates; attribution, baseline comparability, benefit adequacy, duration, and independent verification vary across country projects and result types.
observations.subgroup: People previously excluded from social protection, workers in informal economies, migrants and refugees, persons with disabilities, unemployed people, older people, women, and people facing climate or other crises.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legal coverage is a necessary foundation and may have value before full implementation; effective coverage can take longer because administrative systems, registration, financing, and delivery need to be built.

observations.period: 2021-2025; institutional reform pathway across 50 priority countries

denominator.unit: priority countries in the second phase of the ILO Global Flagship Programme

institutional_results.value: 180 institutional-change results were achieved against an ambition of 80

strategy.value: 48 results concerned adoption or reform of national social-protection strategies, against an ambition of 10

scheme_design.value: 45 results concerned social-protection scheme design or legal reform, against an ambition of 30

operations.value: 87 results concerned operations, administration, and governance, more than twice the anticipated level

mechanism.value: durable coverage depends on a sequence from policy strategy to legal scheme design to operational administration, rather than on a single transfer or announcement

observations.method: Programme monitoring of institutional results across country support organized around three steps: national strategies, scheme design and reform, and operational or administrative strengthening.
observations.uncertainty: Institutional-result counts measure reported change milestones, not automatically sustained funding, service quality, population take-up, or long-term welfare; countries differ in baseline institutions and verification.
observations.subgroup: National social-protection ministries, finance authorities, administrators, workers’ and employers’ organizations, civil society, development partners, and beneficiaries dependent on delivery systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strategy and legal reforms can create coordination and rights foundations even when short-term coverage does not rise; operational improvements may be less visible but more consequential over time.

observations.period: 2021-2025; crisis-responsive and inclusive social-protection system building

denominator.unit: thematic areas supported by the ILO Flagship Programme

life_cycle.value: the programme integrates health care, maternity, unemployment, disability, old age, and other life-cycle risks through contributory and non-contributory systems

excluded_groups.value: the programme explicitly targets informal-economy workers, migrants, refugees, host communities, persons with disabilities, and people facing climate-related and other crises

partnerships.value: the programme coordinates governments, social partners, development partners, international financial institutions, UN agencies, civil society, academia, and workers’ and employers’ organizations

crisis_catalyst.value: the report presents crisis periods as opportunities to strengthen national ownership and reform, while emphasizing that progress remains incomplete relative to global demand

mechanism.value: social protection becomes resilient public infrastructure when financing, law, administration, social dialogue, data, and crisis adaptation are treated as one system

observations.method: Retrospective programme synthesis across thematic support, country engagement, strategic partnerships, resource mobilization, and results management.
observations.uncertainty: The report is a programme retrospective and does not isolate which thematic or partnership intervention caused each outcome; system resilience, inclusion, and crisis effects require longer-term country-level evaluation.
observations.subgroup: Workers in informal employment, migrants and refugees, people with disabilities, women, older people, unemployed workers, crisis-affected communities, and institutions responsible for social-protection floors.
observations.counterinterpretation: International technical and financial support can strengthen systems but may also create dependency, coordination burden, or reform agendas that outpace domestic political ownership and fiscal capacity.

Official DOI for the ILO Global Flagship Programme report.

boundary: This record adds a legal-entitlement-to-effective-access and institutional-sequencing mechanism to the social-protection findings. It is a programme retrospective, not a population-wide causal evaluation or independent verification of every attributed result; the next test is whether country reforms sustain domestic financing, registration, delivery, adequacy, inclusion, and crisis responsiveness after external programme support changes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official ILO PDF and publication page, 2021-2025 people-level impacts, legal versus effective coverage, benefit adequacy, institutional results, three-step reform pathway, thematic inclusion, partnership architecture, crisis lesson, attribution limits, and programme boundary were reviewed.
